newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up sharply, emphasis on switches.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up sharply, emphasis on switches.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended sharply higher on Thursday, as speculators resumed buying after Wednesday's modest setback as concerns about near-term supply tightness continued to fuel bullish sentiment, traders said.
The nearby September contract led today's run-up, gaining 8.25 cents per lb, to end at 208.80 cents, its highest settlement since June 9. September ranged between 209.75 and 199.50 cents.
Second-month December rose 6.00 cents, to 176.25 cents, while the back months closed 1.00 to 3.95 cents higher.

Dealers said much of the day's activity focused on switches. September/December switch, a barometer of near-term availability, widened to 32.55 cents compared with 30.30 cents at the close on Wednesday.
December/March 1998 stretched to 21.25 cents versus 19.20 cents the previous session.
"Obviously, the emphasis was on the spreads," said Prudential Securities analyst Arthur Stevenson. "September raced ahead of December and December pulled ahead of March.

"What does the premium structure tell us? Again there is the availibility of delivery," he said. "Looking at it in the very near-term there will be some tightness when September moves into notice period in about a week-and-a-half."
Stevenson noted, however, that there was some controversy within the industry, with physical coffee traders questioning whether there was a genuine physical tightness.

Some traders expect September's hefty premium to December to attract coffee to the board. Traders speculate that some European trade houses may be tempted to bring some coffee up for CSCE certification.

"(CSCE) stocks have been hovering at the 90,000 level and been relatively static in the last couple of weeks," said Stevenson. "If indeed there is going to be additional supplies, we're going to have to see it soon."
After Thursday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 1,530 60-kg bags as of August 6, to 90,929 bags. An additional 3,218 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

Traders continued to note the market's relatively slim turnover and low open interest, with some traders saying the market could be vunerable to a sharp sell-off. Total open interest as of August 6 stood at 21,510 lots, down 100 lots from the previous session.
"We're dealing with a relatively illiquid situation," said Stevenson. "It could reverse quickly and I do look for the spreads to narrow."
Volume on the day reached an estimated 7,955 lots.
